changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/5905-componentinput-inputtype-tombstone.md`

- names `packages/sdui-parser/src/index.ts` → `packages/sdui-parser/src/index.ts` — edited by this change

  > The write was measured as a no-op before it was deleted, and re-measured on this branch's base rather than inherited from the card. A structural census over every `inputs:` array in the repository (211 regions, all tracked TS/TSX/JS sources) scores `inputType` at exactly ONE authoring site — the `plugin-markdown` registration — against `name` 953, `type` 969, `label` 966, `description` 194, `enum` 119, `required` 86 and `binding` 4 in the same pass over the same regions, so the instrument was not blind. The other 192 in-repo `inputType` hits are a DIFFERENT face: `FormField.inputType` (`zod/form.zod.ts`), the text-input renderer's prop, and `SchemaBuilder.inputType`, none of which sit on a `ComponentInput`. The publication path is unchanged and was re-confirmed: `packages/sdui-parser/src/index.ts` forwards exactly seven keys per input — `name`, `type`, `of`, `required`, `enum`, `binding`, `description` — so an authored `inputType` could not reach the published `sdui.manifest.json` even in principle.

### `.changeset/5905-componentinput-retire-constraint-keys.md`

- names `packages/sdui-parser/src/index.ts` → `packages/sdui-parser/src/index.ts` — edited by this change

  > All four were declared on `ComponentInput` and read by nothing, on either path. No consumer reads them off a `ComponentInput` value, and the manifest serializer (`packages/sdui-parser/src/index.ts`) forwards exactly seven keys per input — `name`, `type`, `of`, `required`, `enum`, `binding`, `description` — so a value authored here could not reach the published `sdui.manifest.json` even in principle. Re-measured on this branch's merge-base rather than inherited from the card: a structural census over every `inputs:` array in the repository (219 regions, all tracked files) scores `min` **0**, `max` **0**, `step` **0** and `placeholder` **0**, against `name` 926, `type` 926, `description` 161, `enum` 114 and `required` 87 in the same pass over the same regions — the instrument was not blind.

### `.changeset/7493-componentinput-retire-label-defaultvalue-advanced.md`

- names `packages/sdui-parser/src/index.ts` → `packages/sdui-parser/src/index.ts` — edited by this change

  > No manifest ever published them, so no consumer could ever have read them. `sdui-parser`'s serializer (`packages/sdui-parser/src/index.ts`) forwards exactly seven keys per input — `name`, `type`, `of`, `required`, `enum`, `binding`, `description` — so a value authored under any of the three never reached `sdui.manifest.json`, the generated JSX `.d.ts`, or a diagnostic; its boundary type has no slot for them; the registry's data-source seam reads `name` only; and neither the designer nor the app-shell inspectors consult registry `inputs` at all. A structural census over every `inputs:` array in the repository (re-measured on this change's merge-base, `name` 951 and `type` 951 as the controls) counted the writes: `label` 908, `defaultValue` 245, `advanced` 9 — written on nearly every registration, read by nothing.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `51c294958` (merge-base with origin/main): 10 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1734 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2338 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36548081825)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5b09969051914b7d166e70d912a7db0ee4d768a0`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #11044 (body; triage `5883977635`; claim `5885808433`; os-dev-report `5887003164`), PR #11072 (body, its 11-file list, the net diff against `main` at the head), the head's check-runs (`filter=latest`) and, for the re-read the `changeset-claim-re-read` bot addresses to the seat, the pending `.changeset/*.md` bodies at the head. Every file quoted below was read at the base `827550193` or at the head through `contents/PATH?ref=SHA`; nothing was checked out, built or run.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-09-29T09:11Z with `filter=latest`: 43 runs, all completed — 40 success, 3 skipped (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard matrix)`), 0 failure, 0 cancelled. Every derived gate family is green: `Type Check`, `Lint`, the eight `Test` shards and `Test (dist pins)`, `Build & E2E`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `README Export Check`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Bundle Analysis`. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts for this record; the findings below are about pending CHANGELOG prose no gate reads.

### ① Derived judgments

Judged member by member against triage `5883977635`:

- **One list, derived once — right.** `packages/sdui-parser/src/validate.ts` exports `SDUI_BASE_PROPS` (name, scope, tsType per `BaseSchema` member); `BASE_PROPS` and `WHERE_UNDECLARED_BASE_PROPS` are derived from it by scope, and `codegen.ts` imports the same list for `emitBaseProps()` and `YIELDING_BASE_PROPS`. The hand-kept `SduiBaseProps` literal in `codegen.ts` is deleted; no second list remains. `scripts/gen-manifest.ts` is untouched and still writes `generateDts(manifest)` to `sdui-intrinsics.d.ts`, so the producer follows without an edit (the dev's zone-2 correction is right).
- **Member 1 — right.** `visibleWhen`, `hiddenOn`, `testId` are `every-node` entries, so `validateTree` skips them before the declared-input lookup and `SduiBaseProps` carries them. Premises hold at the head: `BaseSchema` declares all three (`z.string()`), `SchemaRenderer`'s hide chain evaluates `visibleWhen` first and `hiddenOn` after `hidden`, and it strips `testId` and re-emits it as `data-testid`; the components pin holds that no live registration declares any of the three, so the ruling's "never silence a declared type check" is not touched by this member.
- **Member 2 — right, as ruled.** `name`, `label`, `description`, `placeholder`, `data`, `ariaLabel` are `where-undeclared` entries. The validator's new line skips such a key only when `byName` has no input of that name; where one is declared the key falls through to the existing binding / expression / `checkType` / `checkMemberTypes` path, so a declared typed input wins with its `type-mismatch`. Pinned on a synthetic manifest (six keys, declared vs undeclared, `424242`) and on the live components registry (every declaring registration keeps `type-mismatch` or `invalid-enum`, every other draws nothing naming the key). No declared type check is silenced by this diff.
- **Member 3 — right.** `SduiBaseProps` is emitted from the list (every entry but `type`), and an interface that declares a `where-undeclared` key extends an Omit of `SduiBaseProps` over exactly the keys it declares, so the declared type wins there too and a declared type the base one does not admit is no TS2430. The in-memory `tsc` pin compiles the generated `.d.ts` with zero diagnostics and holds the card's probe: `bind`, `hidden`, `visibleWhen`, `hiddenOn`, `testId` and an undeclared `label` compile on the `list` tag, a near-miss `bindTo` is refused, and a declared array `data` refuses an object where the base `unknown` accepts it.
- **`visibleOn` deprecation warning — right (not added).** Out of scope per triage; the diff adds no diagnostic code.
- **Accept-set changes the diff implies (all named right by the PR body and changeset):** validator: three keys silent on every type (each was `unknown-prop` on every registered type); six keys silent on every type that does not declare them (494 / 506 / 469 / 464 / 490 / 517 of 519 by the dev's census); no existing key's verdict narrows. Generated JSX types: `SduiBaseProps` gains 11 members (`visibleWhen`, `hidden`, `hiddenOn`, `bind`, `testId` and the six), and 15 published interfaces change their `extends` to the Omit form. Public exports: `SDUI_BASE_PROPS`, `SduiBaseProp`, `SduiBasePropScope` added; nothing removed or retyped. The `tsType` values match `BaseSchema` where they are new (`label` / `description` plain string or inline locale map, `ariaLabel` plain string or keyed reference with `key`, `defaultValue?`, `params?`, `data` any); `hidden` is typed `boolean` following its two siblings, see ③.
- **The four consumer controls (dev deviation 1) — each keeps a real control.** `examples/schema-catalog/test/pageheader-with-actions.test.tsx`: the lit control is now `subTitle`, a near-miss of the declared `subtitle` (the `page-header` registration declares `title`, `subtitle`, `icon`, `actions`, `children`; no `subTitle`, no `description`), so it still draws `unknown-prop` from the app's manifest and goes green only if the undeclared-key branch stops running; the added row pins `description` drawing nothing, which is the ruled cost stated as a deliberate pin. `plugin-detail` `detailSectionAuthoredHideEmpty-10485` and `detailSectionAuthoredIcon-9529`: `hideIfEmpty` and `iconName` are declared by no input of `detail-section` (its inputs are `title`, `description`, `icon`, `fields`, `collapsible`, `defaultCollapsed`, `columns`, `showBorder`, `headerColor`, `hideEmpty`) and are in no base-prop scope, so each still draws exactly one `unknown-prop` naming it from the live manifest in the same run. `plugin-dashboard` `dashboardAuthoredInputs`: `dashboard` declares `label` then `description` (its exact published input list is pinned in the same file), so the regex now demands the Omit form in that order and every per-key assertion is unchanged; a regression to the plain `extends` fails the row.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/11044-base-props-one-list.md` declares `@object-ui/sdui-parser: minor`; the PR carries `Clause-②: yes`. Right: an accept set widens on two published faces (the validator and the generated JSX types) and three exports are added, so `yes` with at least `minor` is the rule's own arm; no `major`, no `skip-changeset`. `@object-ui/sdui-parser` is in the fixed group, so the one entry bumps the group; the three consumer packages changed only test files, and the `Changeset Declaration` gate on the head is green.
- The body names what now passes that did not: the three keys on every node (validator and types), `bind` and `hidden` in the types, the six keys where undeclared (validator explicitly; types through the Omit sentence and the closing paragraph that every entry carries its JSX type), the named cost (`description` on `page-header` now silent), and the new exports. It contains no model identifier.
- Re-read of the three pending bodies the bot names (`5905-componentinput-inputtype-tombstone`, `5905-componentinput-retire-constraint-keys`, `7493-componentinput-retire-label-defaultvalue-advanced`): each cites `packages/sdui-parser/src/index.ts` for the seven-key serializer; at the head `manifestFromConfigs` still forwards exactly `name`, `type`, `of`, `required`, `enum`, `binding`, `description`, the diff touches that file only to add three exports, and the census sentences are anchored to their own merge-base. None is made false. `7493`'s "never reached ... the generated JSX `.d.ts`" is about `ComponentInput.label`, which `codegen.ts` still never reads; the new `SduiBaseProps.label` comes from the list, not from an input's metadata.
- The bot states it does not cover a claim spelled as a symbol. Read against that gap, three further pending bodies carry a sentence this diff makes false — findings 1 to 3 below. They publish verbatim into the same release as this changeset (all pending in the same fixed group), and the dev's own test edits show each was measured to go false.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev: the cost of member 2 (undeclaring types silent on the six keys whether or not their renderer reads them; measured on `page-header` `description`; a per-registration refusal of a withheld base key would be a new rule).** Answered: this is the cost triage `5883977635` chose with "base prop only on types that do not declare it", it is pinned, and the PR body and changeset name it. The census of read sites is NOT MEASURED and the refusal-by-registration idea is a new rule: escalated to the seat to route as the dev's class-c out-of-scope finding, not a condition on this PR.
- **Dev: `RecordAlertProps` TS2430 on the real public manifest (`record:alert` declares `visible` as boolean, string or object; `SduiBaseProps.visible` is `boolean`).** Answered: pre-existing at the base and identical at the head, `visible` is `every-node` and gets no Omit; not this PR's. Escalated to the seat for filing (class a, named producer `generateDts`).
- **Dev: declared `every-node` members keep their silenced declared type check (`className` 227, `disabled` 24, `id` 12, `visible` 1).** Answered: pre-existing, outside the six keys the ruling names, and a uniform declared-first rule would flag the predicate `disabled` the renderer honours, so it is a new decision. Noted; no action on this PR.
- **Dev: the JSX surface types `visible`, `disabled` and `hidden` as `boolean` while `BaseSchema` also admits a predicate.** Answered: pre-existing for the first two; `hidden` goes from refused to `boolean`, a pure widening, and a string predicate stays refused by the types while the validator accepts it. Consistent with the siblings; widening the three to admit the string limb is a separate decision. Noted for the seat.
